    Reference and evidence

    Protocol behavior and local mock features are distinguished throughout. This documentation makes no wallet connections or chain requests.

    This reference binds the handbook to the launch-2404 contract release. It is a documentation snapshot dated 25 October 2026, not a live dashboard. Historical wallet examples were captured on 24 October 2026 at Ethereum block 26,264,861; the original deployment check is older. Supply, current oracle prices and newly registered facts must be read again before a live decision.

    The built-in catalog

    There are 25 facts across 13 families, not 25 separate cells. Direct tiers are cumulative. Renderer display choices do not make higher and lower tiers mutually exclusive. This table summarizes predicates; the source recipe and its exact window govern verification. Catalog source.

    IDFactMeaning and evidence class
    101SpawnedJoined WhitelistCurator; direct.
    201Zero-ShotFirst participation by hour 1; direct.
    202Zero-ShotFirst participation in hour 0; direct.
    301HopperAt least 3 deposits; direct.
    302HopperAt least 5 deposits; direct.
    303HopperAt least 10 deposits; direct.

    402BullfrogLargest single send at least 10 ETH; direct.
    403BullfrogLargest single send at least 100 ETH; direct.

    601SwarmedQualifying seat-operation evidence with at least 3 accepted feedback entries under the fixed recipe; panel evidence.
    701UptimeA qualifying deposit during hours 24–65; wallet-specific chain evidence.
    801HoldoutA deposit in hour 64; wallet-specific chain evidence.

    1301PretrainedAccount nonce at least 20 at Curator deployment; panel evidence.

    Swarmed does not prove three distinct jobs, one human per seat, continuous ownership since mint, or current operator status forever. Its result describes its recorded evidence window. Likewise, cumulative refunded deposit flow is not unique capital, current holdings or a donation total.

    Templates and fixed limits

    PropertyThis release
    Public community templatesT1 event count; T2 event-field sum; T3 ranked shared list; T4 historical unsigned view comparison; T5 historical account nonce.
    Catalog-only recipeT6 seat-operation rule; not a public arbitrary-question template.
    Panel size / quorumT1, T2, T4: 5 / 3. T3, T5, T6: 11 / 7. Direct facts: no panel.
    Evidence modeT1–T4: chain. T5–T6: panel. Both modes still rely on oracle attestation.
    Community ID range10001–65534 inclusive: 55,534 possible registrations.
    Rule mutabilityImmutable after registration; corrections need a new ID.
    Name1–32 permitted ASCII characters: letters, digits, spaces, dots and hyphens.
    Item/signatureAt most 256 bytes, with supported exact event/function grammar.
    Event constraintsNamed parameters, no anonymous event, at most 3 indexed parameters; claimant/group field must be an indexed address; sums use unsigned integer fields.
    T1–T4 windowAt least 7,200 blocks inclusive; closing block at least 64 blocks behind the registration height bound.
    T5 windowOne historical block, at least 7,200 blocks old under that bound.
    Shared ranking head1–32 entries; complete canonical answer required.
    Personal requestExactly one fact ID per upgrade call; one pending request per wallet/fact pair.
    Card mintOnce per original wallet, even if the NFT is later transferred.
    Community metadata displayFirst 32 accepted community IDs, in acceptance order.
    Community artworkFirst 39 facts add cell rings; counts from 40 advance the stepped frame.
    Full community credentialsRead verifiedSpecsOf; the 32-entry display limit is not a credential limit.

    These are contract-bound limits, not all of the current IMD service’s request/body limits. Spec grammar, Composer, Renderer, current IMD reference.

    Fees and permanence

    The Registry constants are 0.1 IMD for Mint Card and 6.4 IMD for Mint Rule, plus transaction gas. Solidity spells the 18-decimal unit with the ether denomination in these constants; the payment asset is IMD, not ETH. Oracle requests pay a separately read current Intake price. 0.5 IMD was a historical observation, not a promise in this handbook. Applying a stored shared fact has no additional oracle price; its transaction still needs gas.

    Card and rule fees are forwarded to the configured BurnExecutor. The subsequent bridge and Base burn are asynchronous external steps, not something a Registry receipt proves complete. The Registry itself accepts no ETH. A frontend’s ETH purchase route is a separate funding convenience, with its own execution and price risks. Sponsored claims and holder allowances from older versions are not features of this release. Registry source, release disclosure.

    Recorded oracle facts do not expire merely because the underlying world changes. The signed answer has an acceptance expiry; the accepted stored credential is historical. The Registry has no owner-driven edit, pause or upgrade path. Those properties make the record predictable but make a changed attester, Intake protocol or broken fixed dependency a migration problem.

    Glossary

    TermMeaning in this handbook
    ClaimantThe original wallet whose facts are evaluated.
    ConsumerAn application or contract that applies a policy using those facts.
    PredicateA specific yes/no contract query such as hasTrait(wallet,701).
    Evidence windowThe exact historical blocks the rule examines.
    AttestationThe structured answer authenticated by the configured signer.
    QuorumThe agreement count required by the recipe; not a count of independently proven human operators.
    Merkle rootA compact commitment to an exact leaf set; not evidence that the leaf policy was correct.
    Candidate universeThe addresses a curator actually searched; an essential coverage limit.
    ArtifactA presentation or export, such as a card or list, whose provenance still needs checking.
